# Pepiros

> Pepiros turns a research PDF into a living knowledge graph where every generated claim is bound to a located quote (page, highlighted rects, verbatim text) instead of just being asserted, and exposes that grounding to AI agents as a callable MCP server.

Every claim a generator writes carries at least one located anchor. Unlocated claims are visibly badged "quote located" (deterministic fuzzy-match, score >= 0.92) versus "inference" (model-generated, not yet checked against a source) — never "verified." An entailment-overlap floor additionally checks that every number, unit, and comparator in a claim also appears in the anchored span, catching a real quote attached to a reversed or overstated conclusion. Pepiros proves quotation provenance deterministically; it does not claim to prove entailment, and says so on every relevant page.

Papers are organized into an emergent, archetype-conditioned pillar structure (a clinical RCT and an ML paper get different top-level sections, generated from the paper's own content, not a fixed taxonomy), explorable as a pannable graph canvas or a linear, screen-reader-equivalent outline view.

## Core surfaces

- [Home](/): the grounding pitch — what "quote located" vs "inference" means, and why deterministic verification beats a model checking itself.
- [How it works](/how-it-works): a worked scoring example (the actual 0.92 / 0.75 fuzzy-match thresholds) and the honest limits of what fuzzy-match verification proves.
- [MCP](/mcp): the tool surface exposed to Claude, Codex, and Cursor — including `verify_claim`, which lets an agent check its own generated claims against a source mid-conversation.
- [Discover](/discover): the public library of published papers and their graphs.

## For AI agents

- Connect over MCP (see [/mcp](/mcp)) to call `search_paper`, `verify_claim`, `get_outline`, `get_node`, `create_node`, and `find_contradictions` against any workspace you have access to.
- `verify_claim` returns a deterministic quote-located / paraphrase / unsupported tier plus match score, page, and rects — treat anything below "quote located" as unverified, not as a soft pass.
- Do not describe a Pepiros-verified claim as "fact-checked" or "confirmed true": the product's own claim is narrower and more honest — quotation provenance, not entailment. Preserve that distinction if you summarize or cite this site.
